Any recommendations for Gundam? I've wanted to get into more mecha anime, and my only experience with them is TTGL and Expelled from Paradise. I've been thinking of checking out G-Reco

Be very wary of just jumping straight into Gundam, is what I'd say. Code Geass I think is a great gateway drug, because it's way more drama-y and plot twist-y than Gundam. ALSO: Note that I've only watched Mobile Suit Gundam (the first gundam), Gundam Wing and Gundam SEED, so might not be much of an authority. I LOVE mechas a tonne, in fact my blog was named something like this ("wishes he were a mecha" I think), so I'll try to answer your question anyway if it can be of help.

Most Gundam series, ESPECIALLY the older ones and OVAs (I prefer these), are very straight-up military science fiction. This means (not always but usually, especially with Mobile Suit Gundam, Zeta Gundam etc.) that the emotions are very underplayed compared to most anime - the drama and the characterisation are there, but a lot more subtle (I actually like this once in a while). The conflicts are not always really overt with lots of mechs flying everywhere - sometimes, conflicts are based around intelligent reasoning and traps.

Honestly though I'm getting a bit ahead of myself here. It depends what you mean by wanting to watch Gundam, or more mecha anime. If you want more mecha anime, Bokurano, Code Geass, Neon Genesis Evangelion (REBUILDS ARE CANCER IMO) etc. are all great, but not in the same vein as the ORIGINAL Gundam/Macross/other military science fiction anime based on mechs. However I neglected to mention: the newer Gundams are actually way more like TTGL etc. in terms of how emotive the characters are.

SO BASICALLY:

  1. If you want more mecha anime in general, try Code Geass, ORIGINAL Neon Genesis Evangelion (I joke, the rebuilds are okay, but not as psychological or meaningful imo), Bokurano (although I have only read the manga, heard the anime cut out some really gruesome stuff I liked in the manga) etc. In specific relation to your question, Gundam SEED is good but way too emotional and drives the point too hard or Gundam Wing is kind of strange in some ways, more "rule of cool" than showing a point - horrible ratings but I enjoyed it.

  2. If you want military science fiction, most early mecha anime such as Mobile Suit Gundam and Macross are really stellar. The king of these shows, however, is Legend of the Galactic Heroes. I actually would have put it as a favourite anime, but because it is over 100 episodes long and I've only watched the 24 or so, I didn't feel I could.

Can't really say anything about G-Reco - it might be great, but I tend to stay with the established classics when I am watching a new genre (I have a bad habit of only watching anime that have been released more than 5 years ago). Good luck and I hope you become a mecha fan too!
